proof_roadmap: Adequacy of the comparison functors (proof lines 1019-1022).
difficulty_reason: Let A -> A' be a ring map and F a module-valued functor on Alg_A whose restriction to A'-algebras is adequate and whose value sequence 0 -> F(B) -> F(B tensor A') -> F(B tensor A' tensor A') is exact for every A-algebra B; the lemma asserts that F itself is adequate (statement lines 1002-1016). The proof observes that the two comparison functors B -> F(B tensor A') and B -> F(B tensor A' tensor A') are adequate by the pushforward and base change lemmas, and concludes because F is displayed as the kernel of a map of adequate functors, which is adequate (proof lines 1018-1024). The level is H2: two sentences, but they name exactly which lemmas make each side adequate and point at the exact sequence in the statement that exhibits F as a kernel, which is the reader-checkable content.
